subject.title: [Feature]: Standardize skill data directory convention (configPaths) under ~/.openclaw/

question: Which durable owner/storage contract should OpenClaw support for community skill runtime data: a core filesystem convention, plugin-state or plugin API storage, ClawHub authoring guidance, or no first-class contract for now?
rationale: The report is valid as an ecosystem ergonomics gap, but repository policy treats new config/storage surfaces and plugin/skill API seams as product and compatibility decisions before implementation.

options.title: Design a narrow core contract first
options.body: Define whether skill runtime data is a filesystem artifact, plugin-state API, or manifest/placeholder contract, then implement the chosen shape with docs and upgrade expectations.

options.title: Move to ClawHub authoring guidance
options.body: If maintainers view this as package hygiene rather than a missing OpenClaw API, document the recommended layout for skill authors in ClawHub without changing core.

options.title: Leave current behavior unchanged
options.body: Keep `metadata.openclaw` limited to eligibility/install hints and leave writable runtime data paths to individual skills.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow core contract first
recommendation.body: Define whether skill runtime data is a filesystem artifact, plugin-state API, or manifest/placeholder contract, then implement the chosen shape with docs and upgrade expectations.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has relevant skill install/docs history and is the strongest routing candidate for a product/API storage-boundary decision from the available history.
